sources.title: Cris Pop's TEDx talk: become the change by choosing the harder path, apprenticeship and sacrifice
sources.originalTitle: The world is not your project. You are. | Cris Pop | TEDxAvram Iancu Street
sources.summary: Cris Pop tells three personal stories (a school cheating scandal, seeking an apprenticeship over a corporate job, and working unpaid to save his company's team) to argue that change starts with who you become. It is a mindset and leadership talk, with little tactical growth advice.

principles.text: Don't wait for others to fix things; the change you want exists because someone chose to become the person who acts.
principles.quote: tot ceea ce nu există deja și tot ceea ce, să zic, foarte face să ne plângem uneori sau să fim frustrați, se întâmplă pentru că cineva, undeva, nu a ales să facă schimbarea pe care putea să o facă.

principles.text: Early in a career, seek an apprenticeship under a leader at a small company, not just the default corporate path.
principles.quote: am căutat companii mai mici, contexte în care din om în om să găsesc un lider, cineva lângă care să pot să ajung și să fiu ucenicul lui.

principles.text: Persistence and a willingness to do any work can open doors that no one is offering, even without open roles.
principles.quote: eu vin, stau, vin dimineața, plec seara, spăl pe jos, mătur, nu contează. Sunt dispus să fiu aici.

principles.text: Work compounds even when results are slow; effort put into becoming better is never wasted.
principles.quote: Dar munca niciodată nu minte. Eu până azi încă nu am simțit că cumva am depus un efort degeaba. Poate a durat 3 ani să văd un rezultat, dar mereu contează.

principles.text: Refuse toxic tools others use to climb; how you behave at work carries into the rest of your life.
principles.quote: dacă la muncă o să încep să mă comport așa, munca aia o duc acasă după, la partenera mea, la familia mea, la prietenii mei apropiați.

principles.text: As a founder, honor promises to your team; when cuts loom, take the first hit yourself rather than lay people off.
principles.quote: ar trebui în primul și în primul rând, înainte să-i dau pe ei afară, să mă dau pe mine afară.

sources.title: Cris Pop on building a people-first culture at Thunder and defining success on your own terms
sources.originalTitle: The truth you avoid about yourself | Cris Pop - Thunder x Project H.U.M.A.N #PH01 (Romanian)
sources.summary: Cris Pop, founder of Thunder, explains why he built a company around culture and trust rather than scale or revenue. He covers hiring young people, giving them room to fail, making decisions without overthinking, defining success himself, and why money and growth should follow culture instead of the other way around.

principles.text: Culture comes first; money and business success are a consequence, not a prerequisite.
principles.quote: Pentru că eu nu cred că ai neapărat nevoie de bani ca să faci o cultură sănătoasă. Ba chiar cred că opusul e mai valid

principles.text: Extend trust to new hires up front and give them space to fail; micromanaging kills their creativity.
principles.quote: cea mai simplă și mai banală decizie pe care am luat o și nu o singură dată, ci de mai multe ori a fost să am încredere în oamenii care ni se alătură.

principles.text: People with integrity and curiosity beat any system; weak people will game even a great system.
principles.quote: Oameni care au intenții bune, care au integritate, au caracter, chiar și cu un sistem care poate lasă de dorit sau are probleme, vor face performanță și ba chiar vor îmbunătăți acel sistem.

principles.text: Define success yourself before judging whether you are successful, or you may win at someone else's game.
principles.quote: e mult mai important să l definesc înainte să trag concluzia că sunt sau nu sunt de succes

principles.text: Most decisions are reversible; pick, try, then adjust rather than stalling indefinitely.
principles.quote: decidem, încercăm, putem să schimbăm lucrurile decât să stăm și să așteptăm la nesfârșit

principles.text: Allow chaos at the start of anything new; structure and systems come after you have run a few cycles.
principles.quote: Deci cumva e bine să accepți faptul că o să fie haos la început și să structurezi pe parcurs

sources.title: Cris Pop on hiring for trajectory, measuring outcomes over hours and defining your own success
sources.originalTitle: Why most young people do NOT succeed | Cris Pop - Thunder x Project H.U.M.A.N #PH00 (Romanian)
sources.summary: Cris Pop, founder of Thunder, answers questions from young people about leadership, careers and failure. He argues for judging people by their current reality and trajectory, measuring the outcome of work instead of hours, blaming effort rather than the market, and defining success and direction on your own terms.

principles.text: Hire on who people are today plus their trajectory, not on the potential you project onto them.
principles.quote: încerc să văd cât se poate de transparent și de onest cum sunt oamenii și nu neapărat să proiectez eu niște potențialul lor pentru că făceam foarte des greșeala asta.

principles.text: Measure the outcome of your work, not the hours you put in.
principles.quote: tot mai mult caut să măsor efectiv outcome ul muncii mele. Dacă am stat o o oră și am scris cât de mult am scris și ce calitate are ceea ce am scris și nu să privesc numai că am stat o oră să scriu.

principles.text: Work expands to fill the time you assign it, so set tight deadlines to free up time.
principles.quote: un task tinde să ocupe spațiul pe care noi cumva îl îl asignăm încă dinainte.

principles.text: Young people blame the market for a lack of jobs when the real issue is insufficient effort and the search for shortcuts.
principles.quote: foarte des, ei spun că problema este marketul, dar în realitate din ce îmi dau eu seama, problema sunt ei pentru că nu depun destul de mult efort

principles.text: Failure and success are definitions you set yourself, so set realistic expectations and judge yourself patiently.
principles.quote: până la urmă eșecul e cam ca și succesul. E tot o chestie pe care cred că noi o definim.

principles.text: Choose a direction and stay directionally right; small course corrections compound over months and years.
principles.quote: e foarte important să accepți să fii ceea ce eu numesc cumva directionally right

sources.title: Cris Pop on building Thunder: generosity, personal growth and growing leaders in a team
sources.originalTitle: Business impact through generosity and organizational culture with Cris Pop | Algoritmi Pentru Suflet (Romanian)
sources.summary: Cris Pop, co-founder of the Cluj IT company Thunder, explains how he builds a people-first company. He covers collective learning habits, growing team members into leaders, generosity as a value, never laying people off because of weak sales, and why a business is capped by its founder's growth.

principles.text: A team of leaders with real ownership outperforms a few thinkers directing many executors.
principles.quote: o echipă în care nu știu avem una două persoane care gândesc totul și nu știu 10 care execută pe un model de fabrică și o echipă în care 12 persoane cu responsabilități diferite dar cu leadership puternic pe anumite zone ad că între astea două echipe Nu cred că există un semn de întrebare cine o să câștige

principles.text: Growing other leaders is the highest form of leadership. Overcome the fear of it by experimenting with a small project first.
principles.quote: în a crește lideri văd cea mai înaltă formă de leadership adică aia mi se pare cumva că în momentul în care reușești cu adevărat să crești niște lideri ești să zic așa pe cea mai înaltă treaptă de leadership

principles.text: Make leadership domain-based: the specialist leads on their area, but remains open to feedback and challenge.
principles.quote: avem un coleg care este pur și simplu să zic așa un specialist el știe cel mai bine lucrurile alea asta și acolo El e leer pe domeniul

principles.text: Be generous by aiming to give more than the other person expects, in salary, tools, education and client delivery.
principles.quote: Eu îmi doresc să ridic un pic mai mult lucrurile dincolo de de ceea ce tu te ai aștepta din partea mea ca să simt că am fost cu adevărat generos

principles.text: Never let people go just because sales are weak. The founder owns that responsibility, and joining a team is a vote of loyalty.
principles.quote: nu putem pur și simplu să luăm și să aruncăm oameni din barca noastră Doar după bunul plac și Doar după cum ne merge nouă bine

principles.text: A business is limited by its founder. If you won't grow yourself or let others outgrow you, the ceiling is clear.
principles.quote: business ul în sine este limitat cumva de de fondator sau de de antreprenor sensul că dacă la mână tu nu crezi în evoluția ta și nu investești în evoluția ta și doi la mână dacă nici nu lași alți oameni să crească să fie mai buni decât tine

sources.title: How Cris Pop builds Thunder and its community on generosity, mentoring and values
sources.originalTitle: The value of generosity in the community with Cris Pop and Cristian Popa | Omnia Radio, Conexiuni (Romanian)
sources.summary: Cris Pop explains how Thunder grew from values inherited from his family: generosity, honesty and non-transactional relationships. He covers how mentoring, book gifting and events (Talks, Labs, Lounge) work, why Thunder refuses clients that threaten its culture, and how to start giving back with small steps.

principles.text: Build relationships on shared values, not transactions; commercial opportunities are a side effect of that foundation.
principles.quote: dar cumva asta vine mai degrabă ca un efect a unei baze fundamentale care care pornește De la de la valori și de la principii

principles.text: You don't need to be an expert to mentor; start sharing what you know with people a step behind you.
principles.quote: nu trebuie să fiu nu știu cât de bun sau să am nu știu câți ani de experiență pe pe o anumită zonă ca să pot să încep să dau mai departe

principles.text: Turn down clients and partners who would damage your work culture, even if the money is good.
principles.quote: ar fi însemnat să stricăm cumva cultura de muncă doar pentru profit sau pentru niște bani care vin

principles.text: Community work is a prioritization choice: build the company plan around it, while keeping client value intact.
principles.quote: practic timpul îl găsim pentru că l prioritizăm

principles.text: Don't chase audience size at events; limit growth to connect deeply with each attendee and build a lasting group.
principles.quote: ne interesează să ne conectăm cât mai profund cu fiecare dintre ei să putem să aducem cumva schimbare

principles.text: Start giving back small and local: one hour a week with one person is enough to begin.
principles.quote: nu trebuie neapărat să începi cu un eveniment de 50 de oameni poți să ți faci o oră pe săptămână sâmbăta într o seară să te întâlnești cu un tânăr

sources.title: Employees vs partners: how Thunder builds a value-first team culture
sources.originalTitle: Employees vs partners with Cris Pop and Izabella Geapana | Omnia Radio, Business 360 (Romanian)
sources.summary: Cris Pop, cofounder of Thunder, explains why he treats employees as partners rather than subordinates. He covers delegating, serving the team as a leader, hiring and client choices based on shared values, and choosing slow growth over fast revenue.

principles.text: Delegate and give real freedom; micromanagement turns people into extensions of you and burns you out.
principles.quote: altfel de fapt ajungi să faci micromanagement și oamenii nu prea pot să creze prin aspectele lor unice și mai degrabă î doar o formă de extensie a ta

principles.text: A founder's job is to create the context (resources, knowledge, ideas) so teammates can perform, serving them rather than commanding.
principles.quote: încerc să facilitez tot tot procesul ăsta de muncă și să mă pun cumva în serviciu în serviciul lor

principles.text: Don't try to be the best at everything; be the reference point for values, not for every technical skill.
principles.quote: nu pornesc de la premisa și nu mă prezint în fața colegilor ca și cum eu Ar trebui să fiu cel mai bun la toate lucrurile astea

principles.text: Define values from day zero and hire people who share them; skills alone are not enough.
principles.quote: noi am pornit la la drum cu valorile încă din din ziua zero

principles.text: Say no to clients and growth that conflict with your values; small side steps compound into losing control.
principles.quote: Am fost nevoi să să spunem nu unor posibile cumva colaborări pentru că nu ar fi însemnat un parteneriat în baza valorilor

principles.text: Choose slow, solid growth rooted in culture over fast growth by adding people just to raise revenue.
principles.quote: ne am asumat cumva un slow growth să zic așa o creștere Mai mai mai puțin accelerată dar mai solidă

sources.title: Cris Pop on building a human-centric company: guidelines over rules and a meaningful day
sources.originalTitle: What if life didn't have to compete with work? W/ Cris Pop | Do More, Stress Less
sources.summary: Cris Pop, founder of Thunder, explains why he builds a human-centric culture and runs the team with flexible guidelines instead of rigid rules. He covers strategy trade-offs, protecting deep work blocks, and refusing double standards between founder and team.

principles.text: Set strategy as flexible guidelines, not strict rules, so the team has room to explore, fail and adjust.
principles.quote: I usually try to have this strategy a bit of more like guidelines and less rules, because rules are very strict

principles.text: Accept you can't do everything; pick the best set of trade-offs and commit to it.
principles.quote: there is more work that I than I can do or like more work than the team can do.

principles.text: Aim for a meaningful day (a solid eight), not a perfect ten, to stay predictable and human.
principles.quote: I try to optimize it for having like a meaningful day rather than a perfect day.

principles.text: Do not expect every task to feel meaningful; accept unglamorous work as part of the bigger purpose.
principles.quote: We love it through the big picture cuz we understand it's an it's a needed piece of work so that we can do the whole thing we actually care about.

principles.text: Empower people to decide without waiting on the founder, and keep the same standards for yourself as for the team.
principles.quote: I don't want ever to have double standards in my team.

principles.text: Protect big uninterrupted blocks for creative work and group meetings instead of fragmenting the day.
principles.quote: You need probably bigger blocks of time, 3-4 hours, to just lean into that work and have no distractions.

sources.title: Full of facts, but empty of change: integrate ideas instead of collecting them
sources.originalTitle: Full of facts, but empty of change
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues that learning is not progress unless ideas get integrated into daily life. He re-reads sources until they stop yielding, tests one idea for a week, cuts inputs that don't serve a current problem, teaches only what he has lived, and listens diagnostically to find what people actually need.

principles.text: An insight is worthless until it lives in a system you use every day.
principles.quote: If it doesn’t live in your day-to-day life, it doesn’t live at all.

principles.text: Squeeze one resource dry (re-read, rewatch) before moving to the next.
principles.quote: I usually read the same book a few times.

principles.text: Test one idea at a time by building something around it for a week.
principles.quote: One idea. One week. Build something around it.

principles.text: Cut inputs that don't solve a problem you face right now, even good ones.
principles.quote: Ask yourself, is this solving a problem I’m facing right now?

principles.text: Only teach what you've tested and failed with yourself.
principles.quote: Teach from the scars, not the scripts.

principles.text: Listen diagnostically to find where the real need and confusion live before offering insight.
principles.quote: You can’t teach with precision if you haven’t first listened with obsession.

sources.title: Hooks vs meaning: why Cris Pop argues for anti-hooks and building for humans over algorithms
sources.originalTitle: Every hook is a door. Few lead to meaning.
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues that creators have become obsessed with hooks and thumbnails, trading honesty and depth for algorithmic performance. He proposes "anti-hooks", clear summaries and chapter markers, and serving existing audiences over chasing reach, betting that slower, deeper growth lasts longer.

principles.text: Hooks are bait: they pull people in but rarely deliver the depth that keeps them.
principles.quote: A hook can spark curiosity, sure. But hooks are just bait. They pull you in, but rarely let you stay long enough to find anything real.

principles.text: Optimizing for algorithms instead of humans costs you depth, resonance and meaning.
principles.quote: Because the cost is attention without depth. Reach without resonance. Growth without meaning.

principles.text: Serve the loyal audience you already have rather than chasing people who never stay.
principles.quote: Let’s serve the people already listening, not chase the ones who never stay.

principles.text: Replace manipulative hooks with honest openings: anti-hooks like a quiet question or a single human sentence.
principles.quote: Maybe it’s time we try “anti-hooks” – a quiet question, a single sentence that feels like someone reaching out, a moment of real reflection.

principles.text: Give viewers clarity up front (summaries, topic lists, chapter markers) instead of curiosity-gap traps.
principles.quote: We can give people clarity instead of confusion — with summaries, topic lists, and chapter-like markers that offer a gentle frame instead of a dopamine trap.

principles.text: Build slowly and honestly: it may not go viral, but it goes deep and lasts.
principles.quote: Maybe it wouldn’t go viral, but it would go deep. And maybe that’s the kind of impact that actually lasts.

sources.title: The visible is built on the invisible: small, unseen acts of care compound into culture
sources.originalTitle: The visible is built on the invisible
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues that team culture is built in the background, through small unrequested improvements done with care. He says leaders should notice and name that invisible work, because people rarely know their effort mattered unless told. Feedback should include what was done right, not only what to fix.

principles.text: Real change mostly happens in the background, through people choosing to do small things well with no audience.
principles.quote: But most of the time, real change happens in the background. It’s someone choosing to do something well, even when the only witness is their own integrity.

principles.text: Look for the small details. How small things get done, or don't, shows who you are as a team.
principles.quote: At Thunder, we’ve learned not to overlook the small details. In fact, we look for it. Because the way small things get done (or don’t) says everything about who we are.

principles.text: Small improvements made daily with care compound until they become the culture and the work.
principles.quote: Small improvements, made daily, with care.

principles.text: Don't assume people know their good work landed. Tell them you saw it and that it mattered.
principles.quote: But even the best of us forget to say the most obvious thing: “I saw what you did, and it mattered.”

principles.text: Feedback should celebrate what someone got right, not only point at what's missing or broken.
principles.quote: Where feedback includes not just what to fix, but what you got right.

principles.text: Work is really about building belonging and trust, earned by how people show up for each other in little ways.
principles.quote: We’re building a team where trust is earned by the way we show up for each other, again and again, in the little ways.

sources.title: The other half of learning: extracting lessons instead of consuming information
sources.originalTitle: The other half of learning
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues that growth comes from actively extracting lessons from books, failures and successes, not from passively consuming information. He offers two questions and a habit of honest self-review as the difference between people who change and people who stay stuck.

principles.text: Consuming information is not learning; insights must be actively pulled out and applied.
principles.quote: But just because you’ve consumed the information doesn’t mean you’ve learned the lesson.

principles.text: Treat every experience as raw material you must work on, not something that hands you answers.
principles.quote: Every time you read something, hear something, or go through something hard, you’re being handed raw material. It’s up to you to do something with it.

principles.text: Ask two questions of every experience: what's in it for me, and what do I learn from this.
principles.quote: Two simple questions, ones that many avoid: "What's in it for me?" and "What do I learn from this?"

principles.text: When something fails, ask from ownership and insight rather than blame or self-pity.
principles.quote: This is when you stop asking from a place of blame or self-pity, and start asking from a place of ownership and insight.

principles.text: A course sells you the chance to do the work, not the transformation itself.
principles.quote: you don't pay for transformation, you pay for the chance to do the work.

principles.text: Schedule honest conversations with yourself about what you learned and how you're applying it.
principles.quote: they regularly sit down and have honest conversations with themselves about what they've learned and how they're applying it.

sources.title: Why Cris Pop built The Thunder Way around ordinary people who choose to act
sources.originalTitle: The strength of a society is in what we choose to carry
sources.summary: Cris Pop writes about visiting Dragoș Pătraru's Biblioteca Nației and why he wanted Pătraru as a voice at The Thunder Way's first event. The essay is mostly values-driven, but it holds a few usable founder lessons: build around ordinary people, recruit trusted voices when launching something that matters, and ask for the seemingly impossible.

principles.text: Build around ordinary people: what separates some is choice, not talent or luck.
principles.quote: none of us are born special or destined for greatness. What sets some apart is not talent or luck, but choice.

principles.text: When launching something that matters, recruit trusted voices that carry weight.
principles.quote: When you're building something that truly matters, you need voices that carry weight. Voices that matter in our society, the ones people trust, respect, and feel genuine.

principles.text: Ask for the seemingly impossible; it feels out of reach until you find the courage to ask.
principles.quote: something that seems impossible until you finally have the courage to ask.

principles.text: Invest in people and legacy rather than things you don't need.
principles.quote: He invests in people, in their education, in their growth, in building something that will outlast us all: a legacy rooted in community, knowledge, and care.

principles.text: Integrity means making tough choices daily and choosing what's right even when unpopular.
principles.quote: It means facing the issues most people avoid and choosing what's right, even when it’s not popular.

principles.text: Build what's missing instead of debating what's broken.
principles.quote: While others debate what's broken, he builds what's missing

sources.title: Designing intentional experiences: build for the person on the other side, not the persona
sources.originalTitle: Blueprints of intentional experiences
sources.summary: Cris Pop explains how Thunder Talks events start from an imagined newcomer's feelings rather than logistics or content. He extends the same empathy to feedback and to product or community decisions, asking what the other person actually needs and designing for people instead of personas.

principles.text: Start event design by sitting in the attendee's empty chair, not with logistics or content.
principles.quote: When we organize events, we don't begin with logistics or content. Instead, we sit in an empty chair and imagine: I've never been here before. I'm not sure if I belong. How do I want to be welcomed?

principles.text: Ask what people actually need, not whether they'll like what you built.
principles.quote: Instead of limiting to questions like "Will they like what we've built?", you go deeper and shape what do they actually need. This way, people feel understood before they even realize they needed to be.

principles.text: Design for the quiet introvert in the back row to make participation feel safe.
principles.quote: All of this started by imagining the introvert in the back row, the one who carries a question they won’t ask out loud.

principles.text: Welcome people as friends into your home, with small personal gestures like a book and a message.
principles.quote: We welcome people not as guests, but as friends stepping into our home. We meet them, we try to know them, we do our best to make them feel comfortable.

principles.text: Honest feedback must be effective: shape it so the truth can be received, not just heard.
principles.quote: We don’t have to dilute the truth. We just need to make space for it to land, human to human.

principles.text: Put yourself in the community member's, customer's or attendee's seat to strip away assumptions.
principles.quote: Because when you start from yourself, from your humanness, you begin to strip away assumptions. You stop designing for personas and start designing for people.

sources.title: Cris Pop: The road from knowing to becoming, a personal growth framework
sources.originalTitle: The road from knowing to becoming
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues school fills heads with information but doesn't teach you to build or change. He shares the personal framework he built to outgrow mediocrity: an honest inventory, forgiving and accepting your past, a scout mentality, and small intentional daily steps. Mostly mindset, with little on business tactics.

principles.text: Learning counts only when you put it into practice and live it, not when you store facts.
principles.quote: Learning starts the moment we take ownership of it, when we stop treating knowledge like something to collect and start treating it like something to live.

principles.text: Put intention and passion into your work even if it wasn't your passion at first, or you'll extract only disappointment.
principles.quote: It wasn't my passion at first, but I allowed myself to put passion into what I do because without intention and fire in your work or learning, you'll extract nothing but disappointment.

principles.text: When a task feels too hard, commit to a fixed 1-2 year trial and give it everything before judging.
principles.quote: On my first day coding, I wanted to quit. It was too hard, too confusing. But I made myself a promise: give it everything for 1-2 years and see if I was up for the challenge.

principles.text: Seek mentors, absorb what they offer, apply what fits you, then become a mentor yourself.
principles.quote: I hunted for mentors, people willing to help because when you're truly paying attention, you can learn from anyone walking a similar path.

principles.text: Be a scout, not a soldier: question your beliefs and be willing to be wrong to find the truth.
principles.quote: Stop being a soldier who fights to prove everyone else wrong and start being a scout who's willing to be wrong if it means finding the truth.

principles.text: Take an honest inventory of where you stand, then invest in what you want through small daily steps.
principles.quote: It takes brutal honesty about where we stand, the humility to unlearn what doesn’t serve us, and the courage to take small but intentional steps every day.

sources.title: Strategic quitting: the battle traffic light for choosing which fights to walk away from
sources.originalTitle: The middle ground between success and failure
sources.summary: Cris Pop argues that success/failure is a false binary and that quitting strategically is a real edge. He offers a red/yellow/green "battle traffic light" and a cost-benefit table to decide which fights deserve time, energy and attention, and which to drop.

principles.text: Treat failure as information, not a verdict. Stop forcing what isn't working to make space for what fits.
principles.quote: I don't believe in failure. I believe there is only information. And every time you stop forcing something that isn't working, you're making space for something more aligned with your needs.

principles.text: Stop when you hit the same wall repeatedly. Time, energy and attention are capital; don't spend it on assets that don't grow.
principles.quote: Because why spend capital (time, energy, attention) on assets that don't grow?

principles.text: The binary success-or-failure mindset keeps you stuck fighting battles that no longer matter.
principles.quote: when you're not "winning," you assume you must be "failing." So you keep fighting battles that no longer matter.

principles.text: Push wisely: too little moves nothing, too much breaks things.
principles.quote: Push too little → nothing moves. Push too much → things break. Push wisely → life opens.

principles.text: Strategic quitting is the edge: say no to almost everything so you can say yes to the rare opportunity that changes everything.
principles.quote: The real edge comes from strategic quitting. It's deliberately saying no to 99% of opportunities so you can say yes to the 1% that could change everything.

principles.text: Use a battle traffic light (red, yellow, green) to triage fights; for yellow, compare cost to benefit and move on if cost wins.
principles.quote: If you're in a yellow situation, evaluate the cost vs. the benefit with a simple table

sources.title: Trust over control: how Cris Pop leads Thunder by letting an intern grow beyond her role
sources.originalTitle: Let people tend the roots, and they’ll grow their own becoming
sources.summary: Cris Pop frames his leadership philosophy through an intern story: when Sabina asked to write outside her role, he said yes and the result surfaced a voice that rigid job descriptions would have buried. The essay argues that trust, psychological safety and betting on potential produce stronger people than micromanagement.

principles.text: Leadership means breaking the walls around people, not drawing boxes; nurture raw potential even when it leads somewhere unplanned.
principles.quote: My work as a leader is not about drawing boxes around people. It’s about breaking the walls that confine them.

principles.text: Say yes when someone asks to step outside their role; a request like that is a spark, not a deviation.
principles.quote: I didn’t see it as stepping out of role but a spark beginning to be ignited.

principles.text: Managing by job descriptions and lanes buries valuable voices; listening surfaces what people carry.
principles.quote: If I'd been focused on job descriptions and staying in lanes, if I'd been managing instead of listening, this voice would have stayed buried.

principles.text: Expectations of people are usually too small; give space and bet on potential instead of policing boundaries.
principles.quote: when you bet on potential instead of policing boundaries, you get transformation.

principles.text: Trusted people rise and create things micromanagement can never manufacture.
principles.quote: when people feel trusted, they rise. They don’t just deliver, they soar. They create things no amount of micromanagement could ever manufacture.

principles.text: People grow in freedom, and trust accelerates growth; micromanagement yields workers, trust yields giants.
principles.quote: That people grow in freedom. That trust is the ultimate accelerant.

sources.title: Collaborative entrepreneurship: transparency, shared risk and meritocracy as the base of workplace trust
sources.originalTitle: Collaborative entrepreneurship
sources.summary: Cris Pop recaps a Thunder Talks session with RebelDot's Tudor Ciulean and adds his own view on company culture. The core idea: transparency builds trust, trust builds ownership, and open, meritocratic teams beat "factory culture" companies.

principles.text: Work with people, not for them: share the weight of uncertainty and treat their wins and struggles as yours.
principles.quote: Because when you work with someone, you share the weight of uncertainty. Their wins feel like your wins. Their struggles become your struggles.

principles.text: Lasting business relationships are forged in uncomfortable honesty, not polite half-truths.
principles.quote: Not the easy kind. The vulnerable kind. The kind that risks rejection in order to invite trust.

principles.text: Transparency creates a chain: trust, then ownership, then care and creativity.
principles.quote: Transparency builds trust. Trust fuels ownership. Ownership generates care and sparks creativity.

principles.text: Tell people the real situation, even when it is bad, instead of making false promises, and let them choose to stay or go.
principles.quote: Instead of making false promises, he kept everyone informed about the reality they were facing together.

principles.text: Avoid factory culture that makes people interchangeable; build a meritocracy where the best idea wins regardless of title.
principles.quote: It's built on a meritocratic foundation where the best ideas win, regardless of who suggests them. It doesn't matter if you're the CEO or the newest hire.

principles.text: Give people the why, not just the how; shared understanding of purpose beats a perfect strategy.
principles.quote: Most companies do the opposite. They hide the struggles, micromanage the process, and wonder why people seem disengaged.

sources.title: Cris Pop on human leadership and civic entrepreneurship: how Thunder Talks grew from 4 people to a cinema
sources.originalTitle: An ordinary man who inspires through human leadership and civic entrepreneurship (Thunder Substack Q&A with Cris Pop, in Romanian)
sources.summary: A Romanian Q&A in which Cris Pop explains why he founded Thunder around generosity, self-leadership and civic entrepreneurship. He shows how small, consistent acts and organic community growth (Thunder Talks) beat grand strategies, and why a leader should stay the same person in every role.

principles.text: Nobody will fix your life for you; real change starts when you take your power back (self-leadership).
principles.quote: nimeni nu vine să-ți rezolve viața. Niciun șef, niciun partener și nicio oportunitate magică nu o va face. Singurul care poate schimba ceva ești tu.

principles.text: Teams where people think like leaders and own their results build meaning daily instead of searching for it.
principles.quote: Dacă oamenii încep să gândească ca niște lideri, să-și asume responsabilitate pentru munca și rezultatele lor, sensul nu mai trebuie căutat, ci se construiește în fiecare zi.

principles.text: Start small without a grand strategy and let the community grow organically; you only need the courage for the first step.
principles.quote: Nu trebuie să știm tot drumul, trebuie doar să avem curajul să facem primul pas.

principles.text: Scale in step with real demand: Thunder Talks moved to bigger venues only as people kept coming and bringing friends.
principles.quote: Dar oamenii tot veneau, tot întrebau, tot își aduceau prieteni.

principles.text: Choose speakers with authentic stories who live what they preach, so the community feels close to them.
principles.quote: Ne-am dorit mereu să aducem oameni cu povești autentice, care să fie aproape de comunitate, care trăiesc ce vorbesc.

principles.text: Generosity is the base value: create contexts where people grow, collaborate and support each other, and treat problems as opportunities.
principles.quote: generozitatea nu înseamnă doar să oferi, ci să creezi contexte în care oamenii pot crește, colabora și se pot susține unii pe alții.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Trust yourself first, then let the process breathe; confidence = certainty + faith
sources.originalTitle: Before there’s a path, there’s a pulse.
sources.summary: Andreea Popa argues that teams say they trust the process but treat it like a suspect, confusing control with care. She reframes the problem as self-trust, which she says is built from knowledge, skills and results. She reports Cris Pop sharing a formula at Thunder Talks 10: Confidence = Certainty + Faith.

principles.text: Control is fear of uncertainty and failure; care is patient and spacious, and gives creative work the time it asks for.
principles.quote: Care is patient. Care is spacious. Care means listening when the process says, “I need more time,” and not immediately replying, “Well, we don’t have it.”

principles.text: Over-supervising and rushing the process chokes the life out of the work that makes it powerful.
principles.quote: And the more we try to control the process, the more we choke the life out of it.

principles.text: The real question is whether you trust yourself enough to let the work run without constant supervision, tolerating not knowing.
principles.quote: do you trust yourself enough to let the process work without your constant supervision?

principles.text: Self-trust is built, not felt: from what you know, what you can do and the results you have achieved.
principles.quote: trust in yourself is not only a feeling, but something you build, piece by piece, through experience and results.

principles.text: Cris's formula at Thunder Talks 10: certainty comes from past wins, faith from believing in your potential before there is proof.
principles.quote: Confidence = Certainty + Faith

principles.text: Skill gaps are the next step to grow, not proof you can't be trusted; counter negative self-talk with a 'BUT' that recalls past wins.
principles.quote: “I’m not good at this, but I did X before, and I can learn.”

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Your voice is a place; speak simply from lived truth so people stay
sources.originalTitle: Your voice is a place. Will people stay there or leave?
sources.summary: Andreea Popa argues that sounding smart matters less than being felt, and that a voice is a place people enter and either stay in or leave. She cites Cris Pop's rule from his newsletter, "only teach what you've lived", and builds on it with a case for lived truth and for clarity as respect. Her stories about chasing clever words are her own.

principles.text: Cris's rule: teach only what you have lived, and say it only if it changed you first.
principles.quote: Only teach what you’ve lived.

principles.text: Being understood and changing someone matters more than looking clever; admired but unclear words are not followed or remembered.
principles.quote: People may admire what they don’t understand, but they won’t follow it. They won’t remember it. And they definitely won’t change because of it.

principles.text: Your voice is a place people walk into; if it is not grounded and true, they leave.
principles.quote: Your voice is a place, one people can walk into. Every time you speak or write, you're inviting someone in.

principles.text: Contradicting your own truth costs your message its weight, so stay consistent with what you actually believe.
principles.quote: Break your own truth, and your message loses its weight.

principles.text: Simplifying is respect for the listener, not a dumbing down of complexity.
principles.quote: We don’t simplify because people can’t handle complexity. We simplify because clarity is an act of respect.

principles.text: Speak for the version of yourself who felt small or confused; that is where resonance begins.
principles.quote: Start a piece with a sentence your past self needed to hear.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): If your own story doesn't inspire you, it's time to change it
sources.originalTitle: If your own story doesn't inspire you, it's time to change it
sources.summary: Andreea Popa writes about a line Cris Pop shared with her that changed her mindset: "If your own story doesn't inspire you, it's time to change it." She argues that the narratives we hold about ourselves shape our choices, that one miss shouldn't define us, and she offers reflection questions for rewriting the next chapter.

principles.text: If your own story doesn't inspire you, change it. This is the line the author credits to Cris.
principles.quote: “If your own story doesn’t inspire you, it’s time to change it.”

principles.text: Your story isn't set in stone; you have the power and the responsibility to rewrite the next chapter.
principles.quote: But stories can evolve. And if the current chapter feels uninspiring, you have the power and the responsibility to rewrite the next one.

principles.text: Don't let one missed shot define the whole match; we dwell on misses and forget the wins.
principles.quote: We replay the misses and downplay the wins. We carry the weight of a single moment as if it defines the whole match.

principles.text: Check whether you follow your own path or other people's expectations.
principles.quote: Am I following my own path or what others expect?

principles.text: An uninspiring chapter isn't failure; it signals readiness for growth.
principles.quote: It means you're ready for growth.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Thunder 2025, moving toward what matters before certainty arrives
sources.originalTitle: Thunder 2025: A year written with possibility
sources.summary: Andreea Popa's year-end reflection argues that 2025 was the year Thunder stopped waiting to feel ready and simply began: launching The Thunder Way event, writing the leadership book, and choosing collaboration over competition. It reports Cris Pop speaking at the New York and Cluj events and guiding Thunder Talks conversations, and describes the Thunderometer, a shared values check-in.

principles.text: Momentum comes from showing up fully and trusting your people, not from having everything figured out.
principles.quote: That momentum comes not from having everything figured out, but from showing up fully, believing in what you’re creating, and trusting that the people around you will meet you there.

principles.text: Lead yourself: own quality beyond your tasks, hold standards high, and build with intention.
principles.quote: Lead yourself through the work. Take ownership beyond your tasks, hold your standards high, and build with intention.

principles.text: Treat other companies as collaborators, not competitors, and contribute to a community together.
principles.quote: We’ve never bought into the idea of competition. To us, it’s always been about coming together and contributing to a community worth being part of, side by side.

principles.text: Build community in person: be present where people are and gather them around the same table.
principles.quote: Show up where people are. Pull chairs to the same table, invest in gathering together, and build community the timeless way, close by, present, and reminding one another we’re in this together.

principles.text: Leadership is about being fully human and present, not about titles or authority.
principles.quote: From the truth that leadership is not about titles, nor about authority. It will always come back to showing up, fully human, fully present, and leading from that place of authenticity.

principles.text: Use shared principles as a compass to notice drift, not as rules that dictate what to do.
principles.quote: It doesn’t tell us what to do, but it helps us sense when we’re moving in the right direction.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Guidelines over rules, and handing real ownership to the team
sources.originalTitle: 10 stories from February
sources.summary: Andreea Popa recaps Thunder's February: coaching, culture outings, a hackathon, and the book launch. She reports Cris's coaching question (rules or guidelines?) and that Cris handed interviewing, once mostly his, to Florina, Iuli and Cosmin. She argues growth comes from trust, ownership and consistency.

principles.text: Guidelines create ownership; rigid rules create compliance and box-ticking.
principles.quote: When you lay down rules, people stop feeling like they own what they’re doing. It becomes about compliance, doing something because they’ve been told to.

principles.text: Give people a framework and let them fill in the details; it shifts focus to who they are becoming.
principles.quote: You’re giving them the framework, but they get to fill in the details. And that creates ownership.

principles.text: Transfer ownership fully, including hiring, and trust people to do it well.
principles.quote: The interviews, which had mostly been Cris’s territory until now, were theirs to run. This time, ownership was fully transferred.

principles.text: Growth can't be manufactured; leaders create conditions and then step back.
principles.quote: You can’t manufacture it. You can only create the conditions for it, and then get out of the way.

principles.text: Culture means showing up for a colleague's passion, so it becomes shared.
principles.quote: That’s the culture we’re after, where someone’s passion doesn’t stay theirs alone. It becomes something we all get to experience together.

principles.text: Teaching others, such as interviewing candidates, deepens your own understanding.
principles.quote: Having to explain and clarify ideas for candidates forced him to structure his thinking and revisit fundamentals. Teaching, in a way, became learning.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Let go of the outcome, hold on to the work; self-doubt as a sign you care
sources.originalTitle: March: Self-doubt pulled up a chair
sources.summary: Andreea Popa recounts a March in which Thunder's SXSW event in Austin drew 7 of 70 sign-ups, then Berlin and a home Thunder Talks on self-doubt. She reports Cris opened that talk framing self-doubt as caring and preparing, not something to fight. The post argues for staying in the process, learning rooms by being in them, and treating culture as behaviour.

principles.text: Self-doubt can signal that you care and are ready to prepare and take responsibility, rather than a sign to stop. Cris opened Thunder Talks with this view.
principles.quote: self-doubt can also mean you care, that you’re paying attention, that you’re willing to prepare better, to go deeper, and to take responsibility for what you’re about to do.

principles.text: Don't fight self-doubt; learn to relate to it differently so it becomes part of how you grow.
principles.quote: Self-doubt doesn’t disappear, and maybe it’s not even supposed to. It just changes meaning depending on how you choose to relate to it.

principles.text: When you can't guarantee the result, guarantee your involvement and character (a reframe shared by guest Iulia at Thunder Talks).
principles.quote: “If I can’t guarantee the result, I will guarantee my involvement and my character.”

principles.text: Growth is uneven. Sign-up numbers can mislead, and local knowledge only comes from being in enough rooms.
principles.quote: You learn the room by being in it.

principles.text: Culture is not separate from behaviour; look at how people actually act to understand a team's culture.
principles.quote: Culture is behaviour. How you show up, how you speak, how you treat the person next to you, that’s the culture.

principles.text: Exposing the team to different cultures is how Thunder breaks the ceiling of what it thinks is possible, accepting failure along the way.
principles.quote: We believe that exposing ourselves and our team to different cultures and different ways of thinking is how we break the ceiling of what we think is possible.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Ambition is contagious; the culture around you sets your ceiling
sources.originalTitle: April: Someone forgot to tell them no
sources.summary: Andreea Popa recounts Cris Pop and Anda's three-week US trip (San Francisco, Las Vegas, New York) and argues that surrounding yourself with driven, trusting people lowers your own threshold for action. She reports Cris attended the New Narratives retreat, joined padel games with strangers who became contacts, and that the team met young Cluj founders.

principles.text: The culture you're in shapes the ceiling you believe exists, so deliberately seek environments that expand it.
principles.quote: The culture you’re in shapes the ceiling you believe exists.

principles.text: Fear of the fall can blind you to how far you could go; in Silicon Valley failure is expected and normal.
principles.quote: We’re so busy avoiding the fall that we forget to look at how far we could go.

principles.text: Trust and co-creation build audacity: questions asked with kindness land as support, not criticism.
principles.quote: That culture of trust and co-creation is what feeds the audacity.

principles.text: Stories of principles lived with real stakes teach better than abstractions.
principles.quote: When you see a principle lived out, applied by a human being, in a real situation with real stakes, it just gets more texture.

principles.text: Reject scarcity thinking: helping others go further costs nothing and can change everything.
principles.quote: scarcity was a lie, and that helping someone else go further costs you nothing and might just change everything.

principles.text: Every connection is an unrevealed door; keep meeting people and invite others along once you start.
principles.quote: Every connection you make is a door that hasn’t revealed itself yet. Go further and meet more people.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Travel to learn, share more, and build inner authority
sources.originalTitle: August: Time travel was here all along
sources.summary: Andreea Popa's August newsletter recaps Thunder's trips to Tallinn and Helsinki. She reports that Cris and colleagues went to observe how others build, and Cris concluded Thunder isn't missing much, only consistency and bravery in sharing its work. It also covers Cris's long-term dream of Thunder as a place where people start projects and get mentorship, plus Gabi's reflections on confidence and inner authority.

principles.text: Travel to see how others build, then bring back principles for the inside
principles.quote: He goes out looking for how things work on the outside and returns with a principle for the inside.

principles.text: Thunder already has what it needs; the gap is consistency and bravery in sharing its work
principles.quote: What we need is to be more consistent and a bit braver in getting outside our usual places in order to find out how far we can go and in trying to get more exposure for our work.

principles.text: Share knowledge, not just culture, and say yes before feeling ready
principles.quote: This is also good practice for talking about what we know, being seen, and saying yes even when we don’t feel completely ready.

principles.text: Keep putting yourself out there even when things go well, since good times aren't guaranteed
principles.quote: Meeting new people, sharing what we know, and building future relationships don’t always seem urgent.

principles.text: Cris's long-term dream: Thunder as a place to start projects and get mentorship
principles.quote: That one day Thunder might become a place where people not only come to work but also come to start new projects, meet other people, get mentorship, and find support as their ideas are still taking shape.

principles.text: Inner authority lets people disagree honestly without becoming enemies; relationships can survive truth
principles.quote: And perhaps that is one of the quiet ways in which relationships deepen - by discovering that the relationship can survive truth.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): We're not made to do life alone; people raise each other's bar
sources.originalTitle: July: We’re not made to do life alone.
sources.summary: Andreea Popa's July recap argues that Thunder is built around togetherness: bringing promising people close when paths cross, pairing newcomers so the unknown feels smaller, and caring about people beyond their role. It reports Cris's recurring reminder that "we don't have to fight our battles alone" and that he reminds her what she can do when she forgets.

principles.text: Don't let the moment pass when you meet people who fit the culture; bring them closer and see what becomes possible, even without an announced opportunity.
principles.quote: We never announced an opportunity. We just crossed paths. And when we meet people who feel right for the culture we’re trying to build, we don’t really like letting the moment pass.

principles.text: Cris's recurring message: nobody should fight their battles alone. Support from the leader and peers carries people through hard stretches.
principles.quote: But as Cris always points out, we don’t have to fight our battles alone.

principles.text: Leaders and teammates remind people of their capability when they forget it, and share energy when theirs is gone.
principles.quote: Cris, who reminds me what I’m capable of when I forget.

principles.text: Pair people on new challenges so the unknown shrinks and the win is shared ("look what we did together").
principles.quote: But in a way, the unknown got a little smaller because neither of them had to step into it alone.

principles.text: Care about people beyond the role that brought them in: know their dreams and make room for them to grow.
principles.quote: We want to care about the people we bring close beyond the role that brought them through the door. To know what they dream about, what they hope to build for themselves, and, whenever we can, make a little more room for those dreams to grow.

principles.text: Live in a way that raises the bar for those around you; example-setting is among the most powerful things we can do for each other.
principles.quote: I truly believe that’s one of the most powerful things we can do for each other – to live in a way that raises the bar for the people around us.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Values only count when living them costs you something
sources.originalTitle: We carry values, but do we let them carry weight?
sources.summary: Andreea writes that values are proven only when they are inconvenient; otherwise they are just preferences. She extends this to forgiving others who are still growing, and to choosing what you pay attention to, using David Foster Wallace's "This Is Water". It is her reflection; she only references Cris's earlier newsletter on seeing the invisible.

principles.text: Values are tested by cost: if living them is always easy, they are only preferences.
principles.quote: That's the thing about values - they only mean something when they're tested. If it's always easy, always convenient, maybe it's not really a value yet. Maybe it's just a preference.

principles.text: Real values often feel like choosing against your ego, and many are chosen in solitude.
principles.quote: real values show up when picking them feels like choosing against your ego.

principles.text: Be honest about chasing the feeling of being good versus carrying the weight of living it.
principles.quote: I saw how often I was chasing the feeling of being good, not the weight of actually living it.

principles.text: Extend grace: accept people as they are today, not the version you wish they were.
principles.quote: Can I accept the version of them that exists today, not the one I wish they already were?

principles.text: Forgiveness means not reducing someone to their worst moment.
principles.quote: Forgiveness is not pretending the hurt didn't happen. It's choosing not to reduce someone to their worst moment.

principles.text: Choose your attention deliberately, or the world will choose it for you.
principles.quote: Because if you don't choose your attention, the world will choose for you.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Stop waiting and complaining; lead yourself and build the work you deserve
sources.originalTitle: The world you want is waiting for you to build it
sources.summary: Andreea Popa writes a personal essay about spending three years in work that didn't fit, mistaking inaction for patience and complaint for progress. She argues people hold the pen on their own careers and should invest in skills, network, narrative and standards. Cris Pop is not mentioned; the views and anecdotes are the author's.

principles.text: Patience can become a story that justifies staying still; the price of waiting is only seen after it is paid.
principles.quote: But sometimes, patience becomes the story we tell ourselves to justify staying still.

principles.text: Complaining without action is procrastination that feels productive; real change requires risk.
principles.quote: But complaining without action is just another form of procrastination, a way to avoid the truth that change requires risk.

principles.text: Lead yourself first: shift from asking why it happens to you to asking what you can do about it.
principles.quote: Not "Why is this happening to me?", but "What can I do about this?"

principles.text: Invest in what you control (skills, network, narrative, standards) without waiting for permission.
principles.quote: You don’t need permission to grow.

principles.text: Don't bend yourself to fit every opportunity; look for environments that fit you.
principles.quote: You don’t have to adjust yourself to fit every opportunity. Start looking for the ones that fit you.

principles.text: Change is built from small, consistent actions, starting with what you can carry today.
principles.quote: It's built from small, consistent actions taken by someone who decided they deserved better.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Leadership as the art of becoming someone others want to be around
sources.originalTitle: Utopia lives in the way we lead
sources.summary: Andreea Popa interviews Cosmin, a Thunder team member, about music and utopia, and draws a leadership lesson from it. She argues leadership is a balance of courage and vulnerability, not a set of techniques. It does not report anything Cris Pop said or did.

principles.text: Leadership is the art of becoming someone others want to be around, not a set of techniques to master.
principles.quote: Not as a set of techniques to master, but as the art of becoming the kind of human others want to be around.

principles.text: Good leaders give emotions permission to be real and balance light and dark.
principles.quote: Someone who gives emotions permission to be real. Someone who finds balance between light and darkness.

principles.text: The leaders who stay with us are brave enough to be human and give others permission to be themselves.
principles.quote: they were the ones brave enough to be human. The ones who helped me see possibilities I couldn't see before.

principles.text: Harmony among people matters more than the task itself; people over work you love.
principles.quote: He often says he’d rather do work he doesn’t love with people he cares about than the other way around.

principles.text: Leadership holds a balance between courage and vulnerability, vision and reality, ambition and care.
principles.quote: Not perfect, not free of struggle, but a balance between courage and vulnerability, vision and reality, ambition and care.

sources.title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): We develop leadership by learning to lead ourselves
sources.originalTitle: We develop leadership by learning to lead ourselves
sources.summary: Andreea Popa profiles Manu, a Thunder team member who runs marathons and Spartan races, and argues that leadership grows from practicing self-leadership, not from holding a title. She draws lessons from Manu's answers: keep a plan, push a little further, lift others, believe in yourself, and treat every finish line as a start. The post does not report anything Cris said or did.

principles.text: Leadership is developed by practicing self-leadership, not by holding a title.
principles.quote: We develop leadership not by holding a title, but by practicing the activities that teach us to lead ourselves.

principles.text: Commit to a plan and keep it whatever the conditions; consistency removes excuses.
principles.quote: if I’ve scheduled four runs in a week, I complete them.

principles.text: You can usually go a little further than you think; a small push is often enough.
principles.quote: when you feel like you can’t, you actually can go a little more.

principles.text: Real strength lies in lifting others and sharing a common goal rather than competing.
principles.quote: Nobody competes against each other; we all share the same goal: to finish the race together.

principles.text: Treat each achievement as the start of the next challenge, an infinite mindset that avoids post-goal lows.
principles.quote: There’s no finish line for ambition. Every goal you reach is just the beginning of the next challenge.

principles.text: Discipline becomes freedom, and quiet, lasting leadership comes from steady repeated action.
principles.quote: These are the steps that turn discipline into freedom and action into quiet, lasting leadership.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), Opening Thoughts: leadership is ownership, starting with yourself
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: Opening Thoughts
sources.summary: The opening chapter argues that leadership is not a title or authority but ownership: taking responsibility for who you are and where you are going. Andreea Popa recounts that Cris handed her Jocko Willink's Leadership Strategies and Tactics, which reframed leadership for her. She then argues leaders act where they are, grounded in humility, courage and honesty.

principles.text: Leadership is ownership, not a title or authority.
principles.quote: leadership is not a title, nor is it about authority. Leadership is about ownership. It is about taking responsibility for who you are and where you are going.

principles.text: Lead yourself first; only then can you lead others.
principles.quote: I knew the secret to leadership was to lead yourself first. Then, and only then, can you lead others.

principles.text: Leadership begins when you are needed, not when you feel ready or hold a role.
principles.quote: real leadership doesn’t begin when you’re ready. It begins when you’re needed.

principles.text: Start where you are; permission and polish matter less than presence.
principles.quote: Permission is something you offer yourself when you decide to try, to fail, to grow anyway.

principles.text: Humility, courage and honesty are built through many small daily choices.
principles.quote: Not in a single, defining act. But in a thousand small choices. One moment at a time.

principles.text: Leaders make vulnerability safe by showing their own humanity first.
principles.quote: You lead not by pretending to be invulnerable, but by revealing your humanity and making it safe for others to reveal theirs.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Foundation: leadership is built, not born
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Foundation
sources.summary: The chapter argues leadership is built through self-reflection, purpose, daily action and small acts of care, not inherited or mystical. It reports Cris's formula Confidence = Certainty + Faith, his habit of living one idea deeply, and Thunder's commitment to build, fail, learn and rebuild without waiting for permission.

principles.text: Leadership is built, not born, so it is available to anyone willing to do the work.
principles.quote: If leadership is built, not born, then it’s available to anyone willing to do the work.

principles.text: Start with purpose: why you lead, personally. Leadership without purpose is performance that burns you out.
principles.quote: Leadership without purpose is not quite leadership. It’s more like performance.

principles.text: Self-trust formula Cris shared: confidence is certainty from past wins plus faith in future potential.
principles.quote: Confidence = Certainty + Faith.

principles.text: Commit to build, fail, learn and rebuild without waiting for permission, perfect conditions or complete information.
principles.quote: We’re going to build, fail, learn, and rebuild until we create something that changes lives.

principles.text: Go deep on one idea rather than consuming more; live it, act daily, and teach it to someone else.
principles.quote: Wisdom only becomes transformation when you live it, not when you collect it.

principles.text: Culture comes from people leading by example, not rules or posters; notice and amplify those quietly leading without a title.
principles.quote: The right culture doesn’t come from rules or posters on the wall. It comes from people who lead by example, and that starts with you.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Inner Fire: ownership is a decision, not passion
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Inner Fire
sources.summary: The chapter argues that true inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility, not magnetic passion: a decision to own outcomes regardless of motivation. Andreea Popa describes going first, quiet care, claiming what is "mine to take care of", trusting people, and owning your shadows. It reports that Cris told the team in a growth meeting they were "waiting to be told what to do", sparking a shift to ownership, illustrated by Cosmin's story.

principles.text: Real inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility, a decision to own outcomes, not a passion that burns out.
principles.quote: True inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility. It’s showing up consistently when you least want to, owning outcomes, and carrying weight others won’t bear.

principles.text: Go first: be vulnerable and admit mistakes so others feel safe to try, without waiting for certainty or readiness.
principles.quote: None of us has the right answer when we go first. That’s because going first should not be about certainty but about lighting the path so others feel brave enough to follow.

principles.text: Modern leadership is quiet care: take responsibility for mistakes and ask what would make work easier for people.
principles.quote: Who say, That’s my mistake, even when it’s not technically theirs, because taking responsibility moves things forward, and pointing fingers just keeps us stuck.

principles.text: Ownership grows when someone claims what nobody else wants; shared ownership by everyone means care by no one.
principles.quote: When everything belongs to nobody, nothing gets cared for.

principles.text: Trust people before results; being trusted turns executors into owners who build with you.
principles.quote: It happens the moment someone says I trust you and you realize, maybe for the first time, Oh, I’m not working for them—I’m building with them.

principles.text: Cris named the team's problem: waiting for permission and defaulting to leaders for decisions they should make themselves.
principles.quote: We’re not owning our work. We’re just waiting to be told what to do.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Armor: toughness that protects values, not image
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Armor
sources.summary: The chapter argues that the leader's wall of hidden feelings is defensive armor that makes leaders unreachable, while real mental toughness protects values and stays open to connection. It offers practices for the inner voice, flexibility, fear and recovery, and tells Thunder's story of hitting 2 RON in the account, where it reports Cris carried four projects alone while Adi knocked on every door.

principles.text: Defensive armor protects your image; protective armor guards your values while keeping you open to connection.
principles.quote: What you actually need is protective armor that safeguards your values while keeping you open to connection.

principles.text: Train your inner voice to be honest but never cruel, since it is the loudest voice a leader hears.
principles.quote: Train it. Shape it. Make it honest, but never cruel.

principles.text: Quiet strength beats rigid toughness: bend with the storm but keep your roots deep.
principles.quote: The tree that survives is not the one that tries to stand rigid against the wind. It’s the one that bends with the storm but keeps its roots deep.

principles.text: Fear marks the edge of growth, so get curious about it instead of treating it as a reason to stop.
principles.quote: Fear means you’re standing exactly where your life is ready to change.

principles.text: Recovery after a setback is a rebuild into a new normal, not a rewind to who you were.
principles.quote: Recovery is not a rewind button. It’s a rebuild.

principles.text: At Thunder's lowest point, with 2 RON left, Cris and Adi led by carrying the work and opening doors; the danger is staying down.
principles.quote: The danger is neither in breaking down nor in backing down. The danger is in staying there.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Weapon: Discipline over motivation, built on safety
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Weapon
sources.summary: The chapter argues that motivation is a feeling that vanishes when life gets heavy, and that leaders are built on discipline, which shows up regardless. Andreea Popa writes that discipline needs a settled nervous system, fewer commitments, goals that are truly your own, and pre-made decisions. It closes with Manu's running story. The chapter does not attribute specific statements or actions to Cris.

principles.text: Don't rely on motivation; build systems that work regardless of how you feel.
principles.quote: Build systems that work regardless of how you feel, and follow them whether you want to or not.

principles.text: Discipline fails on chaos; when you miss the mark, restore stability before pushing harder.
principles.quote: Instead of pushing harder when you miss the mark, pause and check what support your body needs. Meet that need first, then try again from a stronger foundation.

principles.text: Discipline means subtracting what doesn't matter; audit your commitments and drop at least one monthly.
principles.quote: every yes you give is a piece of your energy you’re lending out.

principles.text: Drop borrowed ambitions; pursue goals that are truly yours, even if less impressive.
principles.quote: Drop the expectations you inherited but never agreed to. Listen for what’s actually yours, even if it’s less impressive on paper.

principles.text: Anchor effort in a reason that matters at the level of identity, then ritualize showing up.
principles.quote: Dig until you find the reason that actually moves your soul, the one that doesn’t just motivate you for a day but anchors you for a lifetime.

principles.text: Save willpower by deciding once: time-box non-negotiables and pre-decide reactions (if X, then Y).
principles.quote: Instead of asking when you’ll do your work, decide once and repeat daily.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Vision: carry it, live it, leave it open
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Vision
sources.summary: The chapter argues that vision is relational, not a blueprint: a leader carries it rather than owns it, leaves it open for others to shape, and proves it through daily action until it lives on without them. Andreea Popa reports that Cris hires for resonance with what Thunder is building, asking about who someone is more than what they can do technically, and says the vision belongs to everyone.

principles.text: Vision is carried, not owned; speaking it before living it breeds no resonance.
principles.quote: most leaders try to speak their vision before they’ve lived it. People won’t follow your vision if it’s just words or a nicely designed plan. They stay behind resonance, and resonance can’t be faked.

principles.text: Good vision shows people their own worth inside the story.
principles.quote: The moment vision reflects back someone’s worth is the moment it starts to move hearts.

principles.text: Keep vision unfinished so others can shape it and make it theirs.
principles.quote: So leave space. Write in pencil. Create margins where others can dream.

principles.text: A working vision keeps moving without the founder; share the wheel so others learn to navigate.
principles.quote: You’re still steering the ship, sure. But if you’re the only one who ever touches the wheel, no one else is learning how to navigate.

principles.text: Make vision real through one daily embodied act.
principles.quote: Because a vision you don’t walk every day is just a story you tell.

principles.text: Hire for resonance with the mission, since systems can be taught but caring cannot.
principles.quote: you can’t teach someone to care about building genuine community.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Voice: lead by listening and making space, not performing
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Voice
sources.summary: The chapter argues that a leader's voice is not a tool of persuasion or performance but a presence that comes from inner work, honesty and responsibility. It says the strongest voice belongs to the listener, and that leaders should make space for others' ideas rather than be the source of all wisdom. Andreea Popa closes with her own story of seeing, at Thunder, leadership reframed as service rather than dominance.

principles.text: Voice comes from alignment and honesty, not polish; vulnerability signals you speak from what matters.
principles.quote: When your words match your life, people feel that. When there’s alignment between who you are and what you’re saying, humans naturally lean in.

principles.text: Leadership is earning trust so people can bring you their fragile things, not commanding the room.
principles.quote: The work here is not learning how to command a room but to become the kind of human others trust with their fragile things.

principles.text: Listening fully makes you the center of gravity; invite rather than interrupt.
principles.quote: Don’t interrupt, invite. Don’t compete for space, create it.

principles.text: Earn attention by giving it first; trust grows in the pauses where others' thoughts land.
principles.quote: Earn attention by giving it first. The most respected voices are built on trust, and people listen to those who have made them feel truly heard.

principles.text: Use your voice to make people feel more capable, helping them trust their own judgment.
principles.quote: The most powerful thing you can do with your voice is make people feel more capable of handling their challenges, not less.

principles.text: Don't be the source of all wisdom; recognize good ideas in others and help them connect.
principles.quote: Stop trying to be the source of all wisdom. Start being the person who recognizes wisdom when you hear it and encourages others to spread it.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The shield: humility shields leaders from ego
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The shield
sources.summary: The chapter argues the shield a leader needs is humility, which guards against ego rather than hiding humanity. It says to be useful rather than look important, be easy to work with, stay open to being changed, and lift others as you climb. It reports Adi describing Thunder as a village where no one claims the storm as their own.

principles.text: Aim to be useful, not to look important; usefulness is what others actually feel.
principles.quote: Importance is what you claim. Usefulness is what others feel.

principles.text: Being easy to work with is part of leadership; attitude decides whether talent gets invited back.
principles.quote: Your talent might get you in the room, but your attitude decides if you get invited back.

principles.text: A mind full of pride has no room to learn; empty the cup to make space for possibility.
principles.quote: Your cup is either full of pride or full of possibility. It can’t be both.

principles.text: Thunder's stance on inclusion: everyone gets a seat by default, no one fights for one.
principles.quote: We, the Thunders, believe no one should be fighting for a seat at the table.

principles.text: Pay it forward: mentor and open doors for others, since success is never achieved alone.
principles.quote: Success is never a solo act.

principles.text: Humility is a team idea: your strength is multiplied through others, so lead by serving.
principles.quote: Humility is knowing that your strength is multiplied through others.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Compass: you are the compass; keep growing and serving
sources.originalTitle: Leadership Before It Has a Name, chapter: The Compass
sources.summary: The chapter argues that when plans stop holding, a leader's real compass is their own capacity to grow, notice, shift and unlearn, not the strategy document. It urges turning discomfort into a growth signal, acting on lessons rather than collecting them, and choosing the people around you deliberately. It closes with a Thunder story: Thunder Talks, Bookclub and Thunder Lab are meant to build a circle of service, not an audience.

principles.text: A leader's real compass is their capacity to grow and adapt, not a precise plan.
principles.quote: The real compass is not the strategy document. It’s you. Your capacity to grow.

principles.text: People follow leaders who evolve and stay alive amid uncertainty, rather than defend yesterday's map.
principles.quote: Not how precise your plan is, but how alive you are in the face of uncertainty.

principles.text: Treat discomfort as a signal of growth: lean in rather than armor up.
principles.quote: To let the awkwardness be a teacher, not a threat.

principles.text: Learning only counts if it changes how you act; consuming content creates an illusion of growth.
principles.quote: Not “What should I know?” but “Who am I becoming?”

principles.text: Unlearn deliberately: question old beliefs and drives, especially when you feel most certain.
principles.quote: Growth doesn’t live in certainty. It lives in the willingness to question your own compass.

principles.text: Choose your circle with intention; Thunder builds spaces for growing together through service, not for audience.
principles.quote: We’re not trying to build an audience. We’re trying to build a circle.

sources.title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Storm: real leadership is the courage to face the storm inside
